hypotheses.statement: Increasing u increases y (positive steady-state gain): a sustained u>0 drives y above its starting value.
Response has inertia: y does not jump instantly but follows with lag/time-constant on order tens to low hundreds of seconds.
No large dead-zone: u around 0.3-0.4 produces a measurable positive slope, falsified if y stays flat at this level.
At u=0, y decays on its own toward ambient near 0.15-0.17 due to heat loss to the room.
Steady-state y is monotonically increasing and approximately linear in u, with the u needed to hold 0.5 in the mid-range 0.2-0.7.
Sensor noise is small relative to control band width 0.05; repeated readings at settled conditions vary by <0.01.

Response has inertia: y does not jump instantly but follows with lag/time-constant on order 100-200 s; E1 still rising at 250 s and E2 decaying over ~300 s imply settling needs several hundred seconds.

Sensor noise is small relative to control band width 0.05; repeated readings at settled conditions vary by <0.01.
